main.ts.method: Entire source cumulatively read: v24 contiguous lines1-2500, this pass2501-3000,3001-3500,3501-3949. No truncated outputs.

findings: notifyVaultMountAdded consumes only scanner fileCount/folderCount/scanLimitHit; scanner errors go to debug logging. Original caller+scanner controls show one stat failure leaves two of ten files announced and then emits Mounted 0 folders and 2 files without an incomplete/error notice; watcher still starts. Explicit cap has its own warning. Failure visibility is not equivalent to completeness.

Mount injection uses per-ID token checks before notification and final watcher startup, and unload clears tokens. Removal batches 32 in-memory entries, files first then folders deepest-first, identity checks before removal; no source filesystem deletion in this method. Native private-vault event behavior unqualified.

Health checks construct remote adapters; SFTP probes disconnect in finally. Background loop uses setInterval without an in-flight guard or unload/revision checks after asynchronous probes. Possible overlapping/stale health updates are a static observation, not a reproduced native race. Initial failure does not trigger the transitioned-offline Notice unless previous state was true.

reconnectMount returns normally when still unreachable; reconnect-all increments its reconnected count after any normal return. Thus its summary is not intrinsically proof of successful reconnection. Not exercised dynamically here.

saveSettings persists raw persistedMountPoints, stripping transient password/secret/reset/TOC-source fields. It does not serialize the effective settings.mountPoints array ordering: settings drag-drop mutates that effective array, then saveSettings writes raw ordering. Persistence consequence is a source-level finding, not a full UI run.

Import UI increments added after addMount normal return, while addMount can reject validation with a Notice and return normally. Imported count therefore need not equal successful admissions. No import or real file writes performed.

Global ignore UI changes rebuild cache but do not call applyIgnoreListToVault; per-mount Add does. Context-menu ignore mutates the runtime mount then saveSettings instead of the managed-TOC persistence helper; ownership consequences need runtime qualification.

Reviewed rrrah scan.rs VisualReport exposes analysed and issues separately, and ScanError covers budget/cancellation/source failure. This is API/source evidence only, not a new end-to-end proof that every consuming UI surfaces all incomplete work.
